title: The guard: block and swing together, the guard's direction, the parry, overpowering, the clash, the swing's cancel
note: Ours, not the rules package's: every number here is SANDBOX, a development control, until the rules package gives them. The shape is the rules package's (adopted: 'directional sword/shield Block, active weapon-motion Parry, incidental simultaneous attack Clash, Strength-dominant overpowering, small weapon-quality influence and continued single-swing sword contacts through eligible shield/arm/torso surfaces' - windows and formulas candidates only). The design intent: 'I favor being able to block and swing at the same time, so block wouldn't cancel. I do like the idea of a dodge being possible during a swing that cancels the swing'; 'It does need to be somewhat general though, because looking directly at an incoming attack can be problematic when trying to land one yourself. Hence why I was somewhat leaning towards how Mount and Blade does it'; 'I do like the idea of a timed block press as being a more active kind of defense instead of just holding block'. The module's switch guard-off turns all of it off (the earlier build's guard).

traits.note: Strength first for force and hold; Dexterity and Melee are technique (the hold's second term, the parry's whole).

attribute_dice_note: SANDBOX phi for the Attributes in the contest: raw/20, the scale skill.json's contest and the damage pool use (raw 20 is one tabletop dot). The combat rules' newly Embraced Strength 15 is 0.75, the trained guard's 21 is 1.05, elite_stress's 400 is 20.

platform.parry_window_note: SANDBOX (ours): 0.2 to 0.3 s. A blow's active window is about 0.27 s (chrisAttackSword, frames 10 to 18 of 29 at its rate); a window as long as the blow's own lets a press timed to the blow's start meet it without needing a frame-perfect press.
platform.parry_repress_note: SANDBOX (ours): a press opens no new window sooner than this after the last one opened (no parry spam): longer than a quick blow's wind-up (about 0.33 s), so a press cannot be repeated through one blow's approach.
platform.cancel_return_note: SANDBOX (ours): a feint's return to guard, the action channel's own fade-out (1.1's fade, a fifth of a second): as quick as the body lets any motion go.
platform.dodge_let_go_note: SANDBOX (ours): a swing a dodge cancels lets the body go over the channel's cross-fade (0.1 s), so the dodge's motion takes it.
platform.guard_arc_note: SANDBOX (ours; Mount and Blade's automatic block): the guard turns by itself toward a threat whose blow's line is within this either side of the body's facing; a blow from outside it meets what is really in its path.
platform.guard_reach_note: SANDBOX (ours): the chest turns at most 50 degrees (the arms and the blade or shield cover the rest of the arc), bends 25 up (the aim offset's own most) and 35 down (about the knees for a blow at a sword's reach).
platform.guard_speed_note: SANDBOX (ours): a quick forehand strikes about 0.5 s after it begins; at 200 degrees a second the guard crosses from rest to its most turn (50) in 0.25 s, so a blow seen from its start is met and one that changes line late, or comes fast from the arc's edge, can beat it.
platform.parry_speed_note: SANDBOX (ours): during a parry window the guard moves three times as fast (50 degrees in under a tenth of a second): the press's active motion.
platform.guard_stance_note: SANDBOX (ours): a lone weapon's hand moves toward the side a blow comes from (fully at 40 degrees across the line to the foe, where its blade is a beat before it would reach the chest) and up or down with the height it would reach (level at -10 degrees seen from the chest, fully high or low 25 degrees from there), the blade turning upright on that side, across above the head for a high blow, down for a low one. Measured (GuardTests): the combat rules' forehand and backhand at five heights against Christof's broadsword guard 1.3 m away met the blade 3 times in 10 directed, once held still; a shield holder's weapon hand keeps the block's place (moving it met blows with the hand first) and its guard only turns to the foe: 8 of 10 at the guard either way.
platform.parry_rebound_note: SANDBOX (ours): a parried (or clash-deflected) blade springs back further than a held one (the earlier build's 0.15 m tip): turned aside, not just stopped. 2 until then; 1.4 since: the held rebound was made 1.5 times the earlier build's (weapons.json's stop.scaled), and a parry 1.4 times that keeps the parried blade where the earlier build's x2 put it (about 0.5 m for a broadsword's quick blow parried; the ceiling 1.05 m against the earlier build's 1.0) so a parry seen in first person does not throw the arm out of the picture. The switch rebound-two-thirds gives 2 again.

arm_solver.note: Ours, not the rules package's: the engine moves the guarding arm itself (there are no guard or parry motions). A lone blade's raised guard against a blow its owner sees is driven across the blow's predicted path (the swing arc's core run in the simulation: the attacker's clip through its active window at its aim, placed where he stands): the intercept is the soonest place on the path, in front of the defender and outside his body, that the hand can reach before the blade does; the guarding blade lies along the arm's line out to it but crosses the surface the incoming blade sweeps at least least_cross_degrees (so it is met whatever the timing). Off: the module's switch guard-solver-off (the earlier build's composed guard). Platform: src/Vitomir.Platform/Animation/GuardSolver.cs.
arm_solver.hand_speed_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): a held guard tracking drifts with the threat at about a fencer's guard (1-2 m/s at the hand); a parry is a snap of the forearm and wrist (3-5 m/s). A quick forehand's blade arrives about 0.3 s after the blow begins: a guard held from before reaches nearly anywhere in its reach by then; one raised late, or a blow quickened by Celerity, can be beaten.
arm_solver.blade_turn_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): the guarding blade's turn (the wrist and forearm), held and in a parry window.
arm_solver.twist_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): the solver may turn the chest up to 40 degrees beyond the guard's own twist toward the foe, bringing the sword's shoulder toward the intercept: 1.1's block stands the body back with the sword's shoulder drawn 0.37 m behind the feet's place, out of reach of a blow at the left side. Measured (GuardSolverTests, before the read time and the body's cut-off were added): a held broadsword met 13, 13 and 10 of 20 forehands (front, 45 and 70 degrees) without the turn, 17, 18 and 14 with it.
arm_solver.geometry_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): the arm asked for at most 0.95 of its reach; the guarding blade meets with its strong half and middle (0.15 to 0.7 of its length from the guard), the incoming blade's outer half (0.45 to its tip, the part that reaches the body); the crossing at least 35 degrees to the swept surface (at 90, always square across it, the guard stood upright under a level blow, out of reach); the intercept at least 0.25 m from the defender's upright axis (outside the chest; measured from the hips, which 1.1's block steps back), and no place on the path after the blade's outer half comes that near the body is tried (the body would be met first).
arm_solver.shoulder_range_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): the shoulder's range for the guarding wrist, in the body's frame from the hips: at least 0.05 m before them, at most 0.35 m across to the off side, 0.6 to 2.1 m above the feet.
arm_solver.read_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): the guard follows a blow only once it has been under way 0.15 s of its own time (the duelling brain's reaction, the earlier build's react_seconds), so it does not move before the blow shows its line (it must not become an omniscient guard). Measured: little limit for a guard already up (a blocking dummy's lone rapier met 96 % of an untrained attacker's blows in the arena, with it and without it). A blow quickened by Celerity is read as late in its own time and so has less of it left.
arm_solver.timing_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): with no threat seen the solved guard fades back to the composed one over 0.4 s; the blow's path is predicted every 1/120 s of clip time (a tick at 1.1's rate), at most 64 places.

skill.note: Ours, until the rules package gives the curve: no stamina pool kind of system: it is a function of an actor's stats and how capable they are at the various kinds of combat, so a person of high Melee blocks more often. A fighter's technique T = phi(Dexterity) x dexterity_weight + Melee (Brawl bare-handed) - the guard contest's own T (contest.parry), phi = attribute_dice (raw/20) - read through these tables at points (straight lines between, held at the ends); every row is divided by its value at the reference sheet, so the combat rules' trained guard (Dexterity 26, Melee 2: T 3.3) keeps the earlier build's guard exactly. hand: the arm solver's hand speed, blade turn and chest turn (held and in a parry window), and times Celerity's attack factor while it is live (the hand speeds as the swing does). read_seconds: the time a blow is under way before the guard follows it (the earlier build's 0.15 at the reference). guard and parry: the duelling brain's chances of raising its guard against a blow and of parrying it (its blockChance and parryChance, at most 1). react_seconds: the brain's reaction (the earlier build's 0.15 at the reference). error_seconds: the brain's parry press off its time by up to this either way (late or early; not normalised). The module's switch guard-skill-off gives everyone the earlier build's numbers.

reference.note: The combat rules' trained guard (sheets/guard_trained.json): every factor 1 there.

skill.points_note: T: the newly Embraced (Dexterity 23) at Melee 0 is 1.15, at 2 3.15, at 3 4.15, at 5 6.15; the combat rules' townsperson (Dexterity 21, Melee 0) 1.05; the trained guard 3.3; Christof's sandbox sheet (Dexterity 300, Melee 3) 18, held at the last point.
skill.response_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours: tied to general skill, so to melee proficiency, to be tuned; even in KCD the block responses are few): the brain's guard and parry factors (the guard and parry tables below, 1 at the reference) times these, so the chances fall across the board and keep the curve's shape. With the brain's default blockChance 0.5 the chance of raising a guard against a blow is now 0.15 at Melee 0 (a shield only: an untrained fighter raises no blade, blade_guard_least), 0.24 at Melee 2 (the trained guard 0.25) and 0.34 at Melee 5 - against the earlier build's 0.29, 0.49 and 0.68; a brain given parryChance 0.5 (the guard-parry specs) parries 0.10, 0.24, 0.40 of the blows it may (0.48, 0.81). A guard's kind's own blockChance (perception's guard 0.6, the watchman 0.5) is scaled the same. guard-skill-off: the earlier build's (every factor 1, no scale).
skill.blade_guard_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours: people without a shield who are untrained never raise a blade or fists to block or parry - townsfolk, beggars, anyone with Melee 0, Brawl 0 bare-handed; trained fighters do so by this curve; a shield still blocks for anyone carrying one; the player's own guard is unchanged). The least Melee (Brawl bare-handed, as the curve reads it) at which the duelling brain guards with a blade or its fists: 1, the line above anyone with Melee 0, a dot of training. Not the technique T: the combat rules' townsperson (Dexterity 21, Melee 0) has T 1.05 and the newly Embraced at Melee 0 1.15, so a T line between them would be a line through Dexterity, not training; and Dexterity 40 with no Melee would count as trained. Trained by it: the trained guard (Melee 2), sandbox.guard and the watchman (3), the knight (3), Christof's sheet (3), the szlachta (Brawl 2: it has no block motion, so its guard is never seen); untrained: the townsperson, the combat rules' human reference and the newly Embraced at Melee 0. The switch blade-guard-everyone turns the gate off.
skill.shape_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): at Melee 0 (T 1.15) the hand moves at 0.77 of the trained guard's (1.53 m/s held, 3.07 in a parry), reads a blow after 0.23 s, the brain guards 0.58 and parries 0.39 times as often, reacts in 0.23 s and presses within 0.09 s of its time; at Melee 2 (T 3.15) 0.98, 0.16 s, 0.97, 0.96, 0.16 s, 0.04; at Melee 5 (T 6.15) 1.26, 0.11 s, 1.36, 1.62, 0.11 s, 0.02. Steeper below the reference than above it: an untrained fighter is clumsy at guarding (Melee 2 is basic competence), a master is quicker but still beatable by a fast or wide blow (the hand at most 1.45 times, 2.9 m/s held).

brain_pace.note: Ours: most enemies do not attack constantly, there are pauses as well, so nonstop attacking and aggression are not modelled; the spacing about right, a little slower. 1.1's melee AI thinks twice a second and swings again as soon as its reload ends; this is ours. After a run of 1 to run_most blows (drawn evenly as the run begins) the duelling brain pauses for a time drawn evenly from its kind's pause_seconds, counted from the end of its last blow's busy time; during it it keeps at its blade's distance and circles, guards (a shield, or a blade when trained: skill.blade_guard_least), parries and dodges as ever, and does not strike; a clearly better opening - its foe staggered, stunned after its blade was stopped at a guard, or its guard broken - ends the pause at once. All draws from the brain's own stream combat.duel-brain.pace. A person's kind: its sheet's template when templates names it, else a vampire's sheet (Kindred) the vampire kind, else trained or untrained by skill.blade_guard_least. An arena spec may give a fighter's brain its own pace ('pace': 'none' or [least, most]; 'paceRun'). The switch pace-off gives the earlier build's constant aggression. Frenzy is not modelled yet; a frenzied person should take the fierce kind.
brain_pace.run_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): one or two blows, even odds: a single blow and a pair (a combination), neither a flurry; 1.1's own runs are unbroken.
brain_pace.kinds_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (the starting ranges, about a quarter slower than first proposed): townsfolk 2 to 4 s (a frightened amateur's long gathering of nerve: about one blow in four seconds at 1.1's 1.1 s busy time), guards and the watch 1 to 2.2 s (a drilled fighter's measured pressure, about a blow every 2.5 s), Kindred, the szlachta and the frenzied 0.4 to 1.2 s (predators: nearly 1.1's constant pressure, about a blow every 1.5 s).
brain_pace.riposte_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours: the riposte tied to melee proficiency, block responses low as in KCD): an opening during a pause - its foe staggered, stunned after its blade was stopped at a guard, or its guard broken - cuts the pause short only by this chance, drawn once as each opening begins (the brain's stream combat.duel-brain.pace), by the brain's Melee (Brawl bare-handed): straight lines between, held at the ends. An untrained fighter almost never ripostes at once (0.05: one opening in twenty), the trained guard (Melee 2) a third of the time (0.30), a master (Melee 5) usually (0.70; Melee 3, the watchman, 0.43). an earlier build cut every pause at its first opening (1.0 at every Melee): a blocking guard ripostes at once and his pauses vanished (10.7 of 13.4 a bout cut against the newly Embraced at Melee 5).
brain_pace.templates_note: The szlachta's sheet is a mortal's (the module has no ghoul), so its kind is named here; a template not named takes its kind by species and training.

shield_read.note: Ours, until the rules package gives it: skill should tell against a shielded guard; guards are not necessarily hard, but powerful enough that a human or fledgling player does not go wild on the townsfolk. What made skill flat: a carried shield takes 0.38-0.49 of the newly Embraced's swings whatever his Melee, nine in ten of them resting (incidental: the guard had not raised it), held by Strength alone; Melee changed his tempo and his own guard, never where his blow went. The shield read: a duelling brain beginning a blow at a foe who carries a shield reads it with this chance by its Melee (Brawl bare-handed; straight lines between the points, held at the ends; drawn per blow from its own stream combat.duel-brain.shield, never drawn at 0) and aims that blow where the shield is not, as it is held now - over its top when the foe's body rises over_metres or more above it (at over_share of that room: the head and neck over a shield held at the chest), else under its bottom when there is under_metres or more above the lowest aim (0.45 m; the middle of that room), else as drawn. Geometry, not a roll: the blade must still get there, and a guard who raises his shield in time meets it (the guard follows a blow's height). The switch shield-read-off turns it off (the earlier build's brain exactly); guard-skill-off too (it is part of the guard by skill). The player aims his own blows.
shield_read.chance_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): an untrained fighter (Melee 0, below skill.blade_guard_least) swings at what is in front of him and never reads a shield; the combat rules' trained guard (Melee 2) a third of the time; the newly Embraced at Melee 3 half the time (0.5), at Melee 5 four blows in five (0.8). The same shape as the riposte's (brain_pace.riposte: 0.05, 0.30, 0.70).
shield_read.geometry_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): over the shield when 0.15 m or more of the foe (a head and neck's worth) rises above its top, aimed half way up that room; under it when 0.25 m or more (a thigh's worth) lies between its bottom and the lowest aim; the shield's top and bottom are its placed box's highest and lowest corners (a raised shield is read where it is raised). Measured (the earlier build's arena, the newly Embraced against rudolfGuard's resting kite shield): his blows aimed at or above level met the body in 53-86 % of the swings that met anything, those aimed 10 degrees down 19-22 % (the shield 63-70 %).

brain_parry.note: Ours: the duelling brain's parry timed by its hand's travel (the finding: its press mostly fell while its own swing kept its guard down, so it rarely opened a window). It chooses a parry only when its own swing and stun will be over before its press is due, holds its own next blow while the parry waits, and presses arrive_seconds + travel_metres / (the parry's hand speed x its skill's hand) + margin_seconds before the blow's strike mark, at most the parry window (0.25 s) before it, give or take its skill's error. Only with the arm solver (guard-solver-off: the earlier build's brain); the switch brain-parry-fixed gives the earlier build's press (0.25 s before the mark, whatever its own swing).
brain_parry.numbers_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours; measured in a duel, GuardSolverTests.Probe_the_brains_parry_in_a_duel: the windows that opened left the hand about 0.2 s at 4 m/s from the ready stance to the intercept; the best press in the coverage table 0.25 s before the mark). At the reference its lead is the window's 0.25 s (0.05 + 0.2 + 0.03 capped), at Melee 0 too (the hand is late: 0.26 s to travel), at Melee 5 0.24 s.

stagger.note: Ours: the stagger when hit is back. A blow that wounds (a blow soaked to nothing or resisted by low work deals no wound) and a guard overpowered (the earlier build's broken guard; overpowered false turns that off) stagger: the hurt (1.1's hurt clip for the carry) plays for least_seconds + seconds_per_newton_second x the blow's impulse (ContactMade.NormalImpulse), at most most_seconds, cutting short a wind-up or a swing before its strike (the blow lost, as Bannerlord's interruption and 1.1's flinch) and lowering a guard; then it fades out over fade_seconds. The upper body is pushed away from the blow on the side struck: the spine turned about the struck point's lever from the chest (push_chest_metres above the feet) crossed with the push, by push_radians_per_newton_second x the impulse, at most push_most_radians, at its most after push_peak_seconds, sprung back (no overshoot) and let go at push_settle_seconds. No new stagger until guard_seconds after the last one ended: 1.1 waits 3.5 s between flinches and blow quality made wounding blows rarer, so it was seldom seen. The switch stagger-oneone gives the earlier build's flinch (1.1's 3.5 s, no push, the whole hurt clip, 1.3 s).
stagger.hurt_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (the design intent: 'let's go with the full stagger v1.1 base game animation'): whole plays 1.1's hurt clip for the carry whole (39 frames, 1.3 s, as 1.1's flinch played it), the stagger lasting the clip and the fighter busy for the larger of that and what its cut-short swing had left; the push laid over it, the swing cut short, the guard lowered, and no new stagger until guard_seconds after the clip ends. short (the switch stagger-hurt-short, the earlier build's stagger-hurt-clip) cuts the clip at least_seconds + seconds_per_newton_second x the impulse, at most most_seconds; none (the switch stagger-push-only, the earlier build's default) is the push alone, the body upright and in reach. Measured.
stagger.numbers_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): a broadsword's quick blow into the body at 10-30 N s staggers 0.4-0.6 s and pushes the chest 9-20 degrees (a rapier's lighter blade less); 1.1's own hurt clip runs 1.3 s (39 frames), the old flinch's busy time. Why these: Bannerlord's interruption and stagger are short (the attacker's stun on a hit about 0.25-0.5 s, its modders'); a quick blow at 1.1's timing comes 1.1 s after the last, so a 0.6 s stagger and a 0.5 s guard after it mean a single foe at 1.1's tempo can stagger every blow that wounds, yet the struck has at least 0.5 s of its own between staggers; a Celerity foe's quicker blows within the guard wound without staggering again.

give.note: Ours: the defender's give, from Bannerlord's developers' account (no video could be watched): 'both the shield and arm will absorb the impact and bounce back on that side', and 'the visual feedback from a cleaner strike or a heavier weapon will be more prominent'. A blow met at a guard and held, parried or overpowered pushes the guarding hand (a shield's arm for a shield) along the blow by metres_per_newton_second times its impulse (ContactMade.NormalImpulse), within least_metres and most_metres, an overpowered guard overpowered_scale times as far; it springs back critically damped at spring_hertz (furthest at 1/(2 pi f) s). It moves the guard's blade or shield, so contact meets it where it is.
give.numbers_note: ENGINE_SANDBOX (ours): a broadsword (1.4 kg) met at 10 m/s, 14 N s, gives 7 cm; at 25 m/s, 35 N s, the most, 15 cm; a rapier (1.1 kg) at 10 m/s 5.5 cm; at least 3 cm; overpowered x2.5 (to 37.5 cm); 2.5 Hz: furthest at 0.064 s, back within about 0.3 s.

weapon_force.note: SANDBOX (ours): a weapon's heft in the force, a small bounded term beside Strength (the rules package's 'smaller, bounded factor'); by rules/harm.json's class ids, 1 for a one-handed weapon.

force.note: F = budget x (strength_weight x phi(Strength) + weapon_force): the swing's attack budget left scales it.

hold.note: H = strength_weight x phi(Strength) x (shield_factor or blade_factor) + technique_weight x (phi(Dexterity) + Melee); a shield holds twice as well as a blade (braced on the arm). An incidental interception (the guard not raised: no guard's hold bonus) holds by Strength alone times incidental_share, without the technique term: at the combat rules' matched sheets 15 % pushed through against a raised shield's 5 %. Measured first at 0.5 (the earlier build's overpowering run): 40 % of the guard's resting shields were pushed through by the newly Embraced at Strength 15 - more than the 'no hold bonus' asks; 1.0 takes away the bonus and nothing more.

overpower.note: P(overpowered) = F^n / (F^n + (margin x H)^n): a blow needs twice the hold for even odds. At the combat rules' matched sheets (newly Embraced F 1.75 against the trained guard's shield H 3.75) 5 %, his blade guard (H 2.7) 10 %; Strength 42 against the shield 15 %, 200 68 %, 400 89 %; 400 against a blade guard 94 %. The blade goes on with budget x max(budget_least, 1 - margin x H / F).

parry.note: Met in the window and not overpowered: P(parried) = T^k / (T^k + (force_share x F)^k), T = phi(Dexterity) + Melee. The newly Embraced (T 1.15) against the trained guard's blow (F 2.05) 56 %, at Melee 3 94 %; the trained guard against his like 91 %.

clash.note: One paired transaction, one draw u: side a dominates if u < P_a = F_a^n / (F_a^n + (margin x F_b)^n), side b if u >= 1 - P_b; else both stop, or both deflect when their contacts' mean angle is under deflect_below_degrees. Matched forces dominate 11 % each way; 400 against 15 nearly always.

contest.riposte_note: SANDBOX (ours): a parried attacker's recovery is this much longer - the defender's chance to strike first, never a free hit.
contest.broken_note: SANDBOX (ours): an overpowered guard cannot be raised again for this long.
